ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ): it is said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), as in the poet's words:
لَا يَقْرَأْنَ بِالسُّورِ
(they do not recite the sūras).
It is also said that it entered to draw attention to beginning with His name in everything, as the Exalted said: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ». On this view it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «اقْرَأْ مُبْتَدِئًا بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ» (recite, beginning with the name of your Lord).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى (٦) أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنَى (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ رَآهُ): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. he transgresses because of that.
The seeing (al-ruʾya) here is in the sense of knowing, so «اسْتَغْنَى» is the second object.

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ (١٥) نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ (١٦)).
The words of the Exalted (لَنَسْفَعًا): when one pauses on this nūn, an alif is substituted for it, because it is vowelless and the letter before it carries a fatḥa. (نَاصِيَةٍ) is a badal (substitute) for «النَّاصِيَةِ»; substituting an indefinite noun for a definite one became acceptable because the indefinite noun is qualified by an adjective (naʿt).

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ (١٧) سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ): that is, the people of his assembly. «زَبَانِيَة» is of the pattern «فَعَالِيَة», from «الزَّبْن», which is pushing.
